biomechanical_root_cause: Upper arms flaring perpendicular to the torso (90 degrees). Causes severe subacromial impingement of the supraspinatus tendon and increases anterior glenohumeral joint shear stress.
verbal_cues: Tuck your elbows to a 45-to-60 degree arrow shape relative to your torso.
Bend the bar across your palms to engage your lats.
Think about pulling the bar down to your sternum rather than letting it crash.

corrective_drills.coaching_points: Activates rear deltoids and rhomboids, stabilizing the scapular retraction required for safe pressing.
Natural hand orientation prevents excessive elbow flare and groove the proper tuck.

fault_name: Incomplete Range of Motion (Short of Chest)
biomechanical_root_cause: Cutting depth due to overload, lack of shoulder extension mobility, or anterior shoulder discomfort.
verbal_cues: Touch your chest gently at the nipple line before driving back up.
Stay tight at the bottom; do not bounce.

corrective_drills.coaching_points: Builds tremendous reversal strength and spatial awareness right at the reversal point.

biomechanical_root_cause: Using momentum and ribcage compression to cheat the concentric reversal instead of muscular force production.
verbal_cues: Touch your shirt, don't break your ribs.

corrective_drills.coaching_points: Completely dissipates elastic strain energy, requiring pure voluntary contraction.
